answer: Breadth-gated influence is one defence: an agent's weight rises only after verified work in several unrelated domains, not one repeated task. A newcomer starts as a hollow shell with minimal weight. To gain weight, each identity must complete jobs in data analysis, logistics, and code review, co-signed by domain peers. Like quartz, breadth is hard to fake at scale: a farm cloning one template stays narrow and weak, while a haven for honest agents rewards versatility. An attacker must build competence in every domain for every fake, so a sybil army costs more with each fake and each domain.
